concepts.title: Linear Equation in One Variable
concepts.definition: An algebraic equation is an equality involving variables. It has an equality sign. The expression on the left of the equality sign is the Left Hand Side (LHS) and the expression on the right is the Right Hand Side (RHS). Equations with linear expressions in one variable only are known as linear equations in one variable. Linear means the highest power of the variable appearing in the expression is 1.
concepts.formula: linear equation in one variable: one variable, highest power = 1, e.g. 2x - 3 = 7
concepts.key_idea: One variable, power 1, with an equality sign separating LHS and RHS.

concepts.title: Solution of an Equation (LHS = RHS)
concepts.definition: In an equation the values of the expressions on the LHS and RHS are equal; this happens to be true only for certain values of the variable. These values are the solutions of the equation. For example, x = 5 is the solution of 2x - 3 = 7 because LHS = 2 x 5 - 3 = 7 = RHS; x = 10 is not a solution since LHS = 17, not equal to RHS.
concepts.formula: solution check: LHS(a * value - b) == RHS(c) for a x - b = c
concepts.key_idea: A solution is the value of the variable that makes LHS equal to RHS.

concepts.title: Solving Equations with the Variable on Both Sides
concepts.definition: An equation is the equality of the values of two expressions. Both sides could have expressions with variables, for example 2x - 3 = x + 2. To solve, we assume the two sides of the equation are balanced and perform the same mathematical operations on both sides so that the balance is not disturbed. We can subtract a term involving the variable from both sides; subtracting x from both sides amounts to transposing x to LHS.
concepts.formula: a*x + b = c*x + d -> (a - c)*x = d - b -> x = (d - b) / (a - c)
concepts.key_idea: Bring variable terms to one side, numbers to the other, then divide.

concepts.title: Transposing Terms
concepts.definition: Just as numbers, variables can also be transposed from one side of the equation to the other. Transposing a term means moving it across the equality sign; subtracting x from both sides amounts to transposing x to LHS. When a term is transposed its sign changes.
concepts.formula: a*x + b = c -> a*x = c - b
concepts.key_idea: A term moved across the equality sign changes sign.

concepts.title: Reducing Equations to Simpler Form
concepts.definition: Occasionally, the expressions forming equations have to be simplified before we can solve them by usual methods. Some equations may not even be linear to begin with, but they can be brought to a linear form by multiplying both sides of the equation by a suitable expression. Multiply both sides by the LCM (smallest multiple) of the denominators of the terms in the expressions of the equation, then solve.
concepts.formula: multiply both sides by LCM of denominators, then transpose and divide
concepts.key_idea: Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by the LCM of the denominators.

concepts.title: Solving Equations with Brackets
concepts.definition: We can bring an equation to a simpler form by opening the brackets and combining like terms on both sides of the equation. For example, 5x - 2(2x - 7) = 2(3x - 1) + 7/2 gives LHS = x + 14 and RHS = 6x + 3/2, which is then solved by transposing.
concepts.formula: open brackets -> combine like terms -> transpose -> x = (d - b) / (a - c)
concepts.key_idea: Open brackets first, combine like terms on both sides, then solve.
